pages.text: "Mom, I want something sweet!" Big sister Dodo lifted her chin and called from the stream bank. Mom rinsed the water jar. "Wait, just let me wash this." Little brother Mumu splashed his feet from the bank.
Then red berries gleamed in a bush, round as candy. "I know! These are food!" Dodo quickly picked one with a wing. She opened her beak wide to put it in.
Mumu gripped Dodo's wing with both of his. Stream water dripped from his feet. "Wait! You don't know what that is!" Dodo stopped with the berry. "Oh? I know it... or don't I?"

They ran to Mom. Mumu offered the berry. "Can we eat this?" Mom bent her long neck, looked, then shook her head. "This isn't for eating." Dodo scratched her head with a wingtip. "Hee hee. I didn't know it after all."
Mom took dark mulberries from her apron pocket and set them side by side on her wing. "Known berries, unknown berries. Only what we know goes into our beaks."

Mom raised her wings one by one. "One, don't touch unknown things with your wings! Two, don't put them in your beak! Three, curious? Ask Mom!" Dodo lifted her chin and repeated loudly, "Don't know it? Ask first!"

A little later, Dodo saw a gray mushroom beneath the willow. Before, she would have picked it quickly. This time was different! She tucked her wings behind her back. "Don't know it? Ask first!" Then she ran to Mom.
Mom saw it and smiled wide. "That mushroom gives you a tummy ache. Well done asking!" One flick of Dodo's tail. Mumu flapped his feet beside her. "You're great, Dodo!"

Now, seeing something unknown, Dodo first hid her wings behind her back. "One, don't touch! Two, don't put it in my beak! Three, ask Mom!" When Mumu saw something shiny, she spoke first. "Don't know it? Ask first!"
On the way back, Mom hugged both warmly in her wings. "You ran to me without touching it!" Unknown things don't go into your beak. Dodo called, "Don't know it? Ask first!"
